   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From: H. Matthews, HEREFORDSHIRE

Dear Sir,

I have received the January
OUTLET and found it interesting.

However I have a problem!

I recently purchased a second-
hand Star LC 10 printer and have
been unable to print from
Tasword 2 (which I have trans-
ferred from tape to disc). I use
a +3 Spectrum.

Could you or any readers offer
help in this matter?

        Yours faithfully,

           H. Matthews

To H. Matthews from Brian Gaff


Well, firstly, you need to fix
the Tasword 2 colours with
TASCOL(OUTLET 22) as it displays
on the +3 with blue paper. Next,
look in the manual for the
Microdrive mods. Instead of
adding the Microdrive syntax,put
in the +3 version...

 FORMAT LPRINT "c";"u"

Now look at line 250. (It's line
250 in my version, anyway!).
There is a weird RANDOMIZE USR
here that calls code via a DEF
FN. Place a REM before this
second RANDOMIZE command, and
the printout should work.

A word of warning though; search
and replace will crash the +3.
The routines use the area of
memory 255 bytes long from
address 23296, and, as you can
see from the +3 manual, this is
used for vital system variables
in 128K mode. Alter line 3000 so
it never gets used in error, if
you wish.

I hope this helps you out.

                          B.G.

From Edward G. Collier, HEREFORD

I have two problems that I would
welcome help on from Chezron
subscribers who have already
overcome them. The problems are:

1) How to transfer BASIC
programs via RS232 interface
from Spectrum+, Spectrum 128 or
Spectrum +3 to an IBM compatible
PC (I have a Sinclair PC200)

2)When driving a Yamaha keyboard
via the Midi interface of the
Spectrum 128, I can get several
parts on one voice but cannot
play several voices simultan-
eously. Z followed by a number
should do it but so far I have
had no success.
              -Edward G. Collier

Brian Gaff to Edward Collier

You do not actually say why you
want to transfer these Basic
programs to the PC200. I am
certain that this PC will run
the common Spectrum emulators
far to slowly to be worth the
effort! However,if you just want
to store programs on the PC200,
I think the answer lies with
some Dutch software...

P-Filers are programs that
compile a code file that
contains Basic and Code from any
program. This file can then be
sent over the RS232 to the PC
with a program called Specterm
at the Spectrum end, and Telix
on the PC end, using Xmodem.

Before you ask, yes, you can
bring them back the other way!
The speed will be 2400 baud. The
lead you need is called a Null
Modem cable. I have never seen
one with a 128K plug on one end
and a D connector on the other,
but you can get Null adaptors,
so a +2 printer cable and one of
those should work.

Telix is shareware, and most BBs
and software libraries should
have it. Specterm, and the tape
version of the P-filer are on a
PD tape I sell for `1, called
creatively, PD tape 1! See
Outboard for the BG Services Ad.
If you want the complete suite
of Specterms and P-filers,please
write to me for details.   B.G.
                      more...

Garry Rowland to Edward Collier

Without making any assumptions
about what you already know, or
mention elsewhere in your
letter, I would sugest the
following checklist -

1)Is the keyboard multi-timbral?
If the manual has no mention of
this then you'll probably have
to settle for one voice for all
parts.

2)Is the keyboard in the correct
receive mode? The Yamaha PSS 590
(the only one I'm familiar with)
has two operational modes (00
and 99). Mode 00 receives all
transmitted channels on channel
0.

Mode 99 must be used for multi -
timbral operation. Each channel
that is to be used must be
turned on (see keyboard manual).
Note: the keyboard's channel
numbers are one less than
PLAY's. PLAY "Y1" will be
received on Yamaha's channel 0.

3) Is the Z command being used
properly? This may have gone
unnoticed if only voice numbers
1-12 are being used. Two numbers
must be sent.

The Program change code (192 +
PLAY channel number -1), then
the voice number (0-127). Eg.
PLAY "Y4Z195Z86" to change to
voice 86 on channel 4 (3 on
keyboard).

What I'd really like to know is
why you are not using 'Music
Writer?' It's much easier.

If none of the above is of any
help then there is always the
Spectrum Music Club (run by Sean
Sanderson). The address for that
is "Chesters", Chester Lane,
High Bentham, Lancaster LA2 7AN.
This specializes in MIDI
software/hardware for the
Spectrum.

                 Garry Rowland

From Chris Oliver, STAFFS

Recently when attempting to draw
a series of concentric circles
using the ARTIST 1 "CIRCLE"
command, I discovered a bug
which has been corrected in
ARTIST 2 and is easy to overcome
in version 1, once you know
about it.

The problem is that there is a
flaw in the circle routine which
produces circles with the wrong
radius or even none at all.

The routine is supposed to draw
a circle about the reference
cursor, with a radius equal to
the distance between it and the
main cursor.

On investigation it was found
that the circle was actually
drawn through a point dropped
onto a horizontal passing though
the centre point:-



               *<Expected radius
              /.
             / .
            /  .
           /   .
          /    .
  Centre>+_____.<Actual radius


You can demonstrate this by
following the "circle" command
with the "box" command on
Artist 1.

If the main cursor is directly
above the centre point when
"circle" is selected, it will
not appear to be doing anything
at all, although it is actually
drawing a circle of zero radius
(and I'm reliably informed that
if you look closely inside such
a circle, you may be able to
glimpse the fabled Oozlum bird!)


The solution to the problem will
already be obvious to you:- ie..


  To obtain the correct radius,
  always move the main cursor
  horizontally to the reference
  cursor.

I recently encountered problems
with the keyboard for which at
first I blamed the edge conn-
ector as usual0 but it turned
out not to be the main culprit
this time. The symptoms were:-


a) 99% loss of the use of "STOP"
   and of the tiddly thing on
   the same key.
b) 75% loss of the use of "!"
   and of "DEF FN".
c) 50% loss of the use of "_"
   and of "FORMAT".

Then the straw which broke the
camel's back: the OUTLET utility
"SKIPPER" (from issue 9) refused
to load without crashing the
system.

The cause of all this turned out
to be a Datel (Kempston type)
interface which I use with a
'Genius' mouse, and had left
plugged into the through-port on
the side of my Opus drive.
Remove the interface and all
works well again.

Do you think the interface has
developed a fault or are there
known bugs with this type? Could
it be the through-port edge
connector mis-behaving?

          Chris Oliver

Brian Gaff to Chris Oliver

This sounds like a bus-loading
problem to me. However, if the
combination has been working, it
could be that one of your pieces
of equipment is faulty. What
happens without the Opus but
with the mouse interface? That
should prove the point.

It's certainly not a fault I've
heard of on that interface. When
they die, the usual effect is a
locked up machine. Have you
tried the setup with another
Spectrum because the effects you
describe afflicted a 128K
machine I had - with nothing
plugged in? A few months later,
the ULA died! After replacement,
the fault never reappeared. BG.

From:Alan Rutherford,FARNBOROUGH

Dear Ron & Brian,

I have sent you another three
crosswords for OUTLET. There is
one small crib. Can the input
line for entering the clues [in
PROCROSS] be extended? As it
stands at the moment, 24 char-
acters does not leave much
imagination for the clues, and
it makes the crossword that much
easier to solve.

Some months ago in the 'wants'
column of OUTLET, there appeared
one for converting the OCP
assembler to run on OPUS
DISCOVERY, +D and Disciple, or
any computer requiring
microdrive syntax.

I used to use the OCP assembler
a lot, until I got my Opus, and
when it wouldn't load I lost
interest in using it. So without
much ado I sent off the tape +
`1.50 and a S.A.E. and a week or
so later I received my tape back
together with a sheet explaining
the changes.

The changes are minor and
include an improvement in the
printing of the code.The command
has been changed and the print
is in three columns down the
page: a great improvement on the
old version.

Other changes are minor but
usually mean that the drive
number has to be included in the
name of the codefile.

There are two main changes to
the program:

1) the verify function is now
disabled and used to catalogue.

2) the symbol tables are now
given in decimal and in BASIC.

If RUN is typed in after the
assembly the values that are
held in the registers are shown.
This can be a help at times.

If you have the MCTT program on
the tape this will no longer
work, as the code for the
conversion has overwritten the
MCTT program. I have not found
that it made much difference as
I had other programs that did
the same job.

This conversion can be obtained
from Paul Preston, 100 Trelawney
Road, Hainault, Ilford, Essex,
IG6 2NW. Paul requires the sum
of `1.50 + a stamped addressed
envelope together with a tape.

When Paul returned OCP he en-
closed a note saying he had man-
aged to convert 'Laser Genius'
to work on the Opus Discovery.
This program has been driving
people mad, trying to get it to
run on Opus. So, I phoned Paul
and all he wanted this time was
proof of ownership of the 'Laser
Genius' program, a S.A.E, a
formatted disc, and the sum of
`3.00. The proof of ownership
can be a photo-copy of the cover
of the instruction manual.

As you might know, the instruct-
ions for the 'Laser Genius' are
not the easiest to understand.

However, Paul has made the prog-
ram work with the Opus and I am
very satisfied with it.

The assembler is a good one and
has a lot more functions than
the OCP one mentioned above.

So far this has only been
converted for the 48k Spectrum.


The basic loader has been
improved and the bug in the
EXPORT command (which stopped it
from working) has now been
corrected.

The code to access the Opus is
stored in the printer buffer. As
a result,the ZX printer will not
work but people with a proper
printer need not worry: it now
prints using the Opus printer
port and the option to use the
ZX printer has been removed.

I have been playing around with
the 'Genius' for a while now and
I am very pleased with it. I
originally used this with the
m/drive but stopped when I got
my Opus and I had forgotten how
good an assembler this was.

I'll now try to do some more
work with m/c, instead of
slacking and using ready-made
programs.

Sorry to have waffled on like
this, but Paul has done a very
good job on two very good
assemblers, and I now am using
either one. The address is the
same as for the OCP assembler.

         Alan Rutherford

P.S.
Can 'Add-enders' be put onto a
separate disc and sold
separately?

Brian Cavers to Alan Rutherford

Many thanks, Alan.

When I wrote PROCROSS,I gave the
size of the clues a great deal
of thought. After reading your
letter I re-loaded PROCROSS and
gave it a lot more thought. I
came to the same conclusion that
I had originally. The size is
limited by the 32-column screen.
This is reduced to 24 characters
for the clues because 3 are used
for the clue number, 1 for A or
D, 2 for the arrow indicating
direction and 3 for separators:
spaces or a full stop. The arrow
might be reduced to 1 and the
separators removed but this will
still only give 27 and a cramped
display.

Theoretically, I could use a 40-
or 50-column print routine but
the whole of the clue area needs
to be totally re-printed rapidly
at each keypress and any special
routine tends to slow it down.

In addition,any changes made now
would make new crosswords
incompatible with the original
PROCROSS.

I remember being disappointed at
the time I wrote PROCROSS but I
finally had to accept compromise
and settle for 24 characters.
If I ever re-write it for the
SAM COUPE I shall certainly go
for at least 64 column but I
can't really see me extending
the Spectrum version now. Sorry.

We have had previous requests to
put our ADD-ENDERS section on a
separate disc for Opus users. It
is not possible with our limited
time and, even given the time,it
would involve sufficient labour
and costs that we would probably
have to charge about the price
of an issue of OUTLET anyway. It
might,therefore, make more sense
for anyone wanting ADD-ENDERS to
get the tape version. With this
in mind, I agreed(I think it was
in last month's OUTLETTERS) that
anyone willing to organise it
has my permission to buy one
copy of each tape version, put
the ADDENDERS on Opus disc and
copy it ONLY TO OTHER GENUINE
OPUS OUTLET READERS so long as I
am not burdened with any part of
it!                       Brian

 b) if it does then have you got

With my sending you a preview of
my reply to you in last month's
OUTLETTERS I think we may be out
of step with questions and
answers!

Just to recap...

In OUTPUT did you try the POKE I

In BLAST IT, I think you have a

with your printer and I just do
not see any solution. I suggest
you stick with TABLOID!

Sorry, I don't know about Plus 3
versions specifically, only that
there are clearly variations in
different machines.
                        - Brian

From John Hunter, MID-GLAMORGAN

  CALCULATION OF EASTER SUNDAY

I have a formula which will
calculate on what day Easter
Sunday will fall, but only for
the years 1753 onwards. As you
will possibly know, in September
1752 the calendar changed from
Julian to Gregorian by omitting
11 days i.e.
        SEPTEMBER  1752

      SUN         17    24
      MON         18    25
      TUE   1     19    26
      WED   2     20    27
      THU  14     21    28
      FRI  15     22    29
      SAT  16     23    30

My program for Easter Sundays
(only valid for 1753 onwards)is:

940  LPRINT "Easter Sundays":
LPRINT:LPRINT:LPRINT

945 INPUT "1st year ? ";Z, "Last
year ? ";Q

950 LET Y=INT (Z/19): LET A=Z-
(Y*19) : LET B=INT (Z/100): LET
C=Z-(100+B):LET D=INT (B/4): LET
E=B-(4*D):LET G=INT((8*B+13)/25)

955 LET T=19*A+B-D-G+15: LET
X=INT (T/30): LET H=T-30*X: LET
J=INT ((A+11*H)/319): LET M=INT
(C/4): LET K=C-4*M

960 LET S=2*E+2*M-K-H+J+32: LET
W=INT (S/7): LET R=S-7*W: LET
N=INT ((H-J+R+90)/25)

965 LET U=H-J+R+N+19: LET V=INT
(U/32): LET P=U-32*V

967 IF P<10 then let QQ=0: GOTO
973

970 LPRINT P;"/";N;"/";Z: LET
Z=Z+1: IF Z>Q THEN GOTO 980

972 IF Z<=Q THEN GOTO 975

973 LPRINT QQ;P;"/";N;"/";Z: LET
Z=Z+1: IF Z>Q THEN GOTO 980

975 GOTO 950

980 LPRINT "End of run. ":
LPRINT:LPRINT

      ====================

I have included this program in
case anyone is interested and
can possibly add an amendment
that would cover the years prior
to 1753.

Possibly  E. Thomson might have
an interest as he produced
"KWICAL" for OUTLET which gave
the Calendar program to cover
pre-1753 as well as current
calendar dates.

        Yours sincerely,

            J. HUNTER

From Edward G. Collier, HEREFORD

I have two problems that I would welcome help on from Chezron subscribers who have already overcome them. The problems are:
